steps.text: Heat vegetable oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat. Stir sugar into oil with a wooden spoon, stirring constantly, until mixture is a light caramel color, about 10 minutes. Mixture will be very hot.

Stir onion, salt, and black pepper into sugar mixture. Onions will immediately start to caramelize. Stir frequently over medium heat until sugar has dissolved and onions are browned, about 15 minutes.
Pour red wine vinegar into onion mixture; simmer until mixture reaches a jam consistency, about 30 minutes. Let cool to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Onion Jam
raw_recipe.description: This onion jam is made by cooking chopped onions in caramelized sugar until thick and jammy for a deliciously sweet spread for sandwiches or crackers.
raw_recipe.name: Onion Jam

review.reviewBody: When I added the onions to the pan, the sugar syrup pretty much seized to a big clump (I suspect from the water in the onions). I just kept breaking it apart, and it finally melted down. After that, it took about 40 minutes to reach the jam consistency, but it was worth the wait. We had this on sliders, and it was so good. I have some leftover, so I'm going to try it on a cream cheese chunk to have with some crackers. Good job Wendy Marie. UPDATE 4.16.12 Made another batch of this, and slathered it onto a ciabatta roll with turkey, swiss cheese, lettuce & tomato. It was delicious.

Ive made this a handful of times now,with the only change being 2 tsp minced garlic added. First few times I followed directions exactly as is. The other day I did it a bit differently, and I think it came out better. I sauteed the onions first, and once they turned translucent, I added BROWN sugar to them, and a dash of Worcestershire. I find that this gave it a richer taste, and helped it set up better in the end. If your a fan of caramelized onions, this is a jar to keep in the fridge! Don't be afraid to make chopping onions a family affair, because I guarantee you'll want to make more than one jar (works out be about 7-8 smaller onions per 12 oz jar when cooked down)!

Just awesome! After reading reviewers saying that the sugar seized up on them, I simply added it later on in the process. Friends and family beg me for jars of this, and its a huge hit at Charity Bake/Cooking Sales as a condiment. I get asked for it every time now. We use it alongside pork, meatloaf, steak, scrambled eggs, etc. It takes awhile to make but well worth the effort. I prefer using Balsamic vinegar over red wine vinegar also. This is a must try!

Searched through many recipes and decided on this because it was easy. WOW!! It's a keeper. I also agree with another reviewer,next time will chop onions smaller. I'd suggest a 1/4" dice. Mine were 1/2" so halfway through the cooking process, I used a hand masher and mashed them finer. Only had 1/4 cup of red wine vinegar so used apple cider vinegar to make 1/2 cup. Can't be rushed though, it did take about an hour and half from start to finish and worth the time. Enjoy!

Always wanted to make this jam after tasting a commercial British version. I added a large clove of garlic, sautéed the onions before adding brown cane sugar, used 2/3 Cabernet vinegar and 1/3 balsamic and scant 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes. It cooked down to jammy consistency at 25 min. I ladled into 4 x1/2 pint sterilized jars and processed 15 min in boiling water bath. The taste is phenomenal! I am having leftover meatloaf tonight and can’t wait to top it with this delicious concoction. 😋 Edit: I made a second batch today and tinkered with the 1/3 balsamic vinegar part. This time I used white balsamic and 2 TBSp raspberry vinegar to the 2/3 cup Cabernet vinegar. The taste difference was quite striking with subtle but bright fruity notes. I will definitely use this combo again. Amazing difference with different vinegars. Apple Cider vinegar would be very good I think to get this effect. Forgot to mention I also added about 1 tsp Worcester sauce both times.

I have made onion jam before. As another reviewer wrote I sliced onion thinly. I think it helps with carmelizing the onions. I add half white and half brown sugar. This is simple to make and tastes delicious on its own.

I found this recipe last summer and made it after reading all of the comments. I printed out the recipe and took notes. I've made it with red wine vinegar and balsamic and love them both equally. I am making more today because I only have one jar left and that just won't do! I read in another recipe that you can water bath for 5 mins, and that is what I've done. I am going to use brown sugar and apple cider vinegar this time.

This is so good! Used plain old yellow onions (because that's what I had on hand) and it turned out delicious! Gave this four stars because I just changed the way I cooked it - I was nervous to add sugar to hot oil so I added the onions to the oil and let them just start to carmelize. Then I added the vinegar, s+p and brown sugar, and let that cook down to that jam consistency. Yummy! Will definitely be making this again!

TRIPLE IT!!
Followed all the advice and added sugar after onions cooked down - no seizing. Did fine dice. Half and half with brown and reg sugar. Half and half with balsamic and cider vinegars. Added garlic, worcestershire. My daughter's share she requested a bit more sugar. 1 batch does about 12 oz jar. I tripled and got 4 jars.

I made this with brown sugar and added a little chopped bacon and minced garlic. It is wonderful! I used my mandolin and got super thin slices of onion. We took it to the campground and ate it on burgers and brats. My sugar also seized up while cooking but with some patience I worked it out. Great recipe!

One of the things I love about baking and cooking in this computer age is that I can read comments on recipes and know ahead of time what some of the obstacles might be. In the case of this Onion Jam, the comments of others proved invaluable. I made a few changes based on the comments including not to worry when the sugar seizes and that balsamic vinegar could be substituted. Both tips made all the difference in the world. This jam is a delicious - a real keeper.

This recipe has become a regular in my house since I discovered it a few months ago. It’s phenomenal on a sourdough grilled cheese, with Granny Smith apples and Brie! I had to substitute white wine vinegar in place of red this time around as I was out, and it was just as good! Definitely prefer red wine vinegar for sure tho lol. Will continue to keep making!
Great recipe!
very oily
I used red wine and balsamic vinegars. Delicious and worthy of a holiday charcuterie board.

I love this recipe! Takes awhile but it is worth it! We love it on hamburgers as well. My first batch got pretty dark colored and tasted burnt, so be careful not to overcook. A lot of crazy looks when asked what I was making. I plan to give some for Christmas gifts this year. Thanks for sharing the recipe.
Love it

I made this today for an upcoming reunion with my sisters. I'm confident that they'll enjoy the flavors. I followed the recipe exactly as written, but doubled it. I'll serve it with my breakfast ham and egg sliders and then leave the remainder of the jar with my sister who is hosting.

Comes together quite well and fairly easily. I did the onions first, then added sugar, but would like to try as the recipe indicates next time, doing the sugar first. Great condiment to elevate an otherwise ordinary meal,

The notes really helped me get through what I otherwise would have feared was me ruining it, haha. The recipe turned out deliciously, a perfect offering on a holiday platter or as a gift for the onion-lover in your life who has everything!
